note:
A SAMPLE deck for local and staging databases, so boxes have cards to pay while the real deck
(the 287 researched cards) is prepared. Not for production: these cards are marked signed off
only so they can drop in a test. The points are approximate; check each one before any card goes live.

cards.name: Balogun Market
cards.fact: One of the biggest markets in Lagos, spread across the streets around Balogun Street on Lagos Island, known for fabrics.
cards.question: What is the best thing you ever bought at Balogun?
cards.visit_tip: Go early on a weekday, before the crowd and the heat.

cards.name: Freedom Park
cards.fact: A park and arts venue on Broad Street, built on the site of the colonial-era Broad Street Prison.
cards.question: Which show at Freedom Park would you take a friend to?
cards.visit_tip: Weekend evenings often have live music.

cards.name: Tafawa Balewa Square
cards.fact: It stands on the old Lagos Racecourse, where Nigeria's independence was celebrated on 1 October 1960.
cards.question: What do you think the crowd felt on 1 October 1960?

cards.name: Nike Art Gallery
cards.fact: A five-storey gallery in Lekki founded by the artist Nike Davies-Okundaye, holding thousands of works by Nigerian artists.
cards.question: Which piece would you hang in your room?
cards.visit_tip: Entry is free; give yourself an hour for all five floors.

cards.name: Lekki Conservation Centre
cards.fact: A nature reserve run by the Nigerian Conservation Foundation, with one of the longest canopy walkways in Africa.
cards.question: Would you do the canopy walk, or watch from the ground?
cards.visit_tip: Wear trainers and bring water for the walkway.

cards.name: National Stadium
cards.fact: The National Stadium in Surulere opened in 1972 and hosted the 2nd All-Africa Games in 1973.
cards.question: What match would you bring back to the National Stadium?

cards.name: National Theatre
cards.fact: The National Arts Theatre in Iganmu opened in 1976, built to host FESTAC '77.
cards.question: What would you stage in the main hall?

cards.name: FESTAC '77
cards.fact: The Second World Black and African Festival of Arts and Culture, held in Lagos in 1977.
cards.question: If FESTAC came back this year, who should headline?

cards.name: Computer Village
cards.fact: One of the biggest phone and computer markets in Africa, in the streets around Otigba Street in Ikeja.
cards.question: What is the most Computer Village thing that has happened to you?
cards.visit_tip: Know the price before you go, and test before you pay.

cards.name: Tejuosho Market
cards.fact: One of the main markets of Yaba, on the mainland.
cards.question: What do you always buy in Yaba?

cards.name: Yaba College of Technology
cards.fact: Founded in 1947, it grew out of Yaba Higher College (1932), the first higher education institution in Nigeria.
cards.question: Who is the most famous Yabatech graduate you know?

cards.name: University of Lagos
cards.fact: The University of Lagos, at Akoka, was founded in 1962.
cards.question: What is the best spot on campus?

cards.name: Fela Anikulapo-Kuti
cards.fact: Fela Anikulapo-Kuti pioneered Afrobeat in Lagos in the late 1960s and the 1970s.
cards.question: Which Fela song would you play first?
cards.visit_tip: The card sits at the Kalakuta Republic Museum, his old home in Ikeja.
